ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is olive-brown with dark spots and a pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a robust body, granular skin, and fully webbed toes adapted for high-altitude streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana chayuensis* is best distinguished by the presence of numerous prominent, black-tipped tubercles scattered across its dorsal surface, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana chayuensis* inhabits high-altitude streams and rocky riparian zones in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chayu Paa frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage along rocky mountain streams for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana chayuensis* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August). They lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana chayuensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting high-altitude streams between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Chayu Paa Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard while calling from rocky streams within its montane forest habitat.
